Castle at Night by Mogens Skjold

the combination of a suppressed coup across the river territories, a spree of raiders ending a large amount of trading connections, and a scandalous marriage for king rogers daughter was an, aromatic mixture. one that dictated details, down to the ways neighbors looked at each other when two would grab for the same whatsit at the local market.

it was traces king roger saw every day as he went down through the streets, carried on his royal litter. he used to love seeing his subjects, now he had armed guards around him then, and didn't know how long he could keep stepping out of his castle. but worrying was straggling. mind drifting to the present, the moonlight snaked through a few hatched windows, and he sulked as he reviewed the royal records with his wine goblet next to him.

his minister of the occult tiptoed in, breaking concentration, and roger was glad to have something else to deal with besides keeping the kingdom from debt. he leaned back, he had known his minster long enough that the pleasantries weren't necessary.

the minster began, thumbing at his necklace, a string carrying pieces of bones too tiny to come from anything comforting, "i found a possible way out of this slump, sire". "thank the gods" king roger said with relief. the mister continued "but, you may not like it", he waved a hand and another figure stepped in. an old woman, eyes bone white and shiny. she wore old rags and clutched a long wooden case.

this tale has been told for centuries hence. the old woman was an eternal enigma since that day, the cases contents nearly broke the kingdom.
